    Storage health¶

    Can each scope's drives hold a continuous recording, and are they healthy? This notebook measures the sustained write speed of the experiment SSD and the OS SD card, how long single writes take, whether a 15.7 MB/s recording would keep up, and whether everything written reads back intact.

    Analysis written by Claude (Anthropic); conceptualised and verified by Yatharth Bhasin.

    Protocol¶

    Acquisition: scripts/debug/storage_health_statistics.py, create_exp() then start_acq_blocking(). No acquisition may run at the same time. About 60–70 min per scope.

    The SSD gets up to 20 files of 9.45 GB (one real 10-minute split each), written in 64 MiB chunks with an fdatasync after every chunk, so each timing is the drive's and not the page cache's. Writing stops before the drive is 85% full. Every chunk is then read back and checked against its CRC. The SD card gets one 1 GB file. SMART is read before and after, with the drive idle; fstrim runs at the end; all test files are deleted.

    Each run folder also holds the files the analysis uses:

    • raw/<disk>/chunks.csv: one row per 64 MiB chunk: file, chunk, t_start_s, write_ms, mb_s, cum_gb, read_ms, crc_ok. Each write is timed up to its fdatasync. All the plots below use this file.
    • storage_health.json: drive identity, SMART before and after, per-file results, kernel storage errors and fstrim.
    • raw/<disk>/smart_before.txt, smart_after.txt: the full smartctl output.
    • telemetry.csv: one row per second per drive from /proc/diskstats; kernel.log: kernel messages.

    def find(d, pattern):
    hit = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "**", pattern), recursive=True))
    return hit[0] if hit else None

def load(row):
    c = pd.read_csv(find(row.dir, "sda/chunks.csv"))
    c["write_s"] = c.write_ms / 1000
    c["minutes"] = c.t_start_s / 60
    return c

W = {k: load(r) for k, r in runs.iterrows()}
J = {k: json.load(open(f"{r.dir}/storage_health.json")) for k, r in runs.iterrows()}
dev = lambda k, disk: next(x for x in J[k]["devices"] if x["device"]["name"] == disk)
pd.Series({k: len(w) for k, w in W.items()}, name="SSD chunks").to_frame().T

    Write speed as the drive fills¶

    Most SSDs first write into a fast cache (flash used one bit per cell), then slow down once it is full. A flat line at the start that drops to a lower one shows where the cache ran out, and the lower line is the speed a long recording actually gets. Repeated swings between high and very low speed mean the drive pauses to empty its cache while still writing. A scope with no run in DATA gets an empty panel. A drive that starts slow has no cache to run out of, and its cache size is left blank.

    Copied! 
    def cache(w, drop=0.5, win=32):
    """GB written before the 32-chunk speed first falls below half the opening speed, and the speed after it."""
    s, gb = w.write_s.to_numpy(), w.cum_gb.to_numpy()
    roll = win * CHUNK_MB / pd.Series(s).rolling(win).sum().to_numpy()
    below = np.flatnonzero(roll < drop * 16 * CHUNK_MB / s[:16].sum())
    if not len(below):
        return np.nan, len(s) * CHUNK_MB / s.sum()
    cut = below[0] - win // 2
    return gb[cut], (len(s) - cut) * CHUNK_MB / s[cut:].sum()

cache_tab = pd.DataFrame([cache(w) for w in W.values()], index=runs.index,
                         columns=["cache_gb", "post_cache_mb_s"])
cache_tab.round(1)

    How long single writes take¶

    The distribution of the time each 64 MiB chunk took to reach the drive, on a log axis. A curve that rises steeply in one place means a steady drive. A long tail to the right is stalls. One chunk holds about 4.3 s of video at 15.7 MB/s, so chunks slower than that are moments the drive fell behind real time.

    Would a recording keep up?¶

    A recording produces 15.7 MB every second. While one chunk takes t seconds to write, the recording adds 15.7 × t MB and the drive takes one chunk away. Count how much would be left waiting. Zero means the drive kept up. Tall or long peaks are data a recording would have to hold in memory until the drive caught up.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    def queue(write_s, rate=REQ):
    q, out = 0.0, []
    for t in write_s:
        q = max(0.0, q + rate * t - CHUNK_MB)
        out.append(q)
    return np.array(out)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(12, 5), sharex=True, sharey=True)
behind = {}
for ax, s in zip(axes.flat, SCOPES):
    for (sc, run), w in W.items():
        if sc == s:
            q = queue(w.write_s.to_numpy())
            behind[(sc, run)] = q.max()
            ax.plot(w.minutes, q, color=COLORS[s], alpha=1 / run)
    ax.set_title(s)
for ax in axes[1]:
    ax.set_xlabel("minutes into the write test")
for ax in axes[:, 0]:
    ax.set_ylabel("MB waiting")
fig.tight_layout()
    def queue(write_s, rate=REQ): q, out = 0.0, [] for t in write_s: q = max(0.0, q + rate * t - CHUNK_MB) out.append(q) return np.array(out) fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(12, 5), sharex=True, sharey=True) behind = {} for ax, s in zip(axes.flat, SCOPES): for (sc, run), w in W.items(): if sc == s: q = queue(w.write_s.to_numpy()) behind[(sc, run)] = q.max() ax.plot(w.minutes, q, color=COLORS[s], alpha=1 / run) ax.set_title(s) for ax in axes[1]: ax.set_xlabel("minutes into the write test") for ax in axes[:, 0]: ax.set_ylabel("MB waiting") fig.tight_layout()

    Read-back¶

    Every chunk is read back from the drive, not from memory, and checked against its CRC. One point per file; the box shows the median and interquartile range for each scope. The USB bridge, not the flash, usually sets the ceiling here, so drives behind the same bridge should line up.

    Copied! 
    def ident(k, r):
    sd, ssd = dev(k, "mmcblk0"), dev(k, "sda")
    smart = open(find(r.dir, "sda/smart_before.txt")).read()
    fw = re.search(r"Firmware Version:\s*(\S+)", smart)
    trim = J[k].get("fstrim", {}).get("sda", "")
    trim = trim.get("supported") if isinstance(trim, dict) else "trimmed" in trim
    b, a = ssd["smart_before"], ssd["smart_after"]
    f = ssd["workload"]["files"]
    return {"model": ssd["identity"].get("model"), "firmware": fw.group(1) if fw else None,
            "bridge": ssd["identity"].get("bridge"), "trim": trim,
            "slowest_file_mb_s": min(x["mean_mb_s"] for x in f),
            "worst_chunk_s": W[k].write_s.max(),
            "chunks_over_real_time": int((W[k].write_s > RT_S).sum()),
            "lifetime_tb_written": ssd.get("lifetime_written_tb"),
            "page_cache_room_mb": J[k].get("page_cache", {}).get("freerun_mb"),
            "read_mb_s": np.median([x["read_mb_s"] for x in f]),
            "crc_bad": sum(x["chunks_bad"] for x in f),
            "smart": b.get("health"),
            "smart_worse": any(a.get(c, 0) > b.get(c, 0) for c in
                               ("realloc", "pending", "media_errors", "crc_errors")),

    Acceptance¶

    Per scope, for the experiment SSD:

    Criterion Level
    Any chunk reads back wrong (CRC) FAIL
    SMART not PASSED, or reallocated, pending, media or link-CRC errors rose during the run FAIL
    A kernel storage error or reset on the drive during the run FAIL
    Speed after the cache runs out below 3 × 15.7 = 47 MB/s FAIL
    A 15.7 MB/s recording would have more waiting than the page cache holds before Linux throttles writers FAIL
    A 15.7 MB/s recording would have more than 2 s of video (31 MB) waiting WARN

    WARN is informational: this test bypasses the page cache, but a real recording writes through it, so anything below the page-cache room (page_cache_room_mb, read from the scope's vm.dirty_* settings) is absorbed without the recording ever waiting. TRIM and the SD card figures are reported but not judged: most USB bridges do not pass TRIM, and the SD card holds the OS, not recordings.
